classes.purpose: Config record for a Hunter-Rank (HR) level: the requirements/thresholds to advance to a given HR level. Consumer computes HR level-ups. Only manager accessors + one evaluator recovered.

methods.purpose: Registers/returns the CInfoManager singleton for CHRLevelInfo.
Thin getter: returns *manager when arg==0 else 0.

Reads the HR cap from CAttributeInfo id 0x13d (attr+0xd0), then walks HR levels upward from current+1 via the paged manager map; each candidate requires HRLevelInfo+0x14 (>0 => required exp/points must be met) and HRLevelInfo+0x18 (a prerequisite/condition id validated by FUN_114cdd70). Advances HR level while conditions hold and triggers level-up.
Iterates every HR level and runs per-level init (FUN_11a08460).
Iterates every HR level and runs CMHLevelInfo per-level init (11a08370).

fields.note: required exp/points to reach this HR level (checked >0 then compared with player value)

formulas: HR cap = CAttributeInfo(id=0x13d).field_0xd0; level-up loop advances from current+1 while requiredValue met and prerequisiteId satisfied, not exceeding cap

Builds a candidate list from a weapon def (param_2, count at [0xf]) into a vector of 0x18-byte entries, then for each candidate rolls a random value between min and max: value = max - rand01*(max-min), where rand01 = FUN_100ee450()*const. notes: Every method in this batch was auto-mislabeled 'CX::GetManagers'. Two boilerplate CInfoManager accessors recur in most classes: (1) the base @-address that lazily registers the singleton via StcMbrNameSvr<CInfoManager>::GetSingletonName / FUN_11679e10 and returns the manager (renamed GetInfoManager); (2) a thin 'return *mgr if arg==0 else 0' getter (GetInfoManagerInstance). All remaining methods are consumers/iterators that carry the real game logic. Manager container layout (verified repeatedly): flat-vector = mgr+0x14 begin / +0x18 end, count=(end-begin)>>2, elem=*(begin+i*4); paged id->object map = mgr+0x20 page-array / +0x24 capacity / +0x28 pageSize / +0x30 minId, index=(id-minId), obj=pages[index/pageSize][index%pageSize]; vtable+0x28=GetCount, vtable+0x18=GetId. No CX::DebugFormat printer or CX::Read_0x99 loader was present in these bundles, so struct field names/offsets are inferred from consumer access patterns (mostly medium/low confidence) except where a matching Tlv doc corroborates (CEquipPlanInfo/TlvEquipPlan, CGuideBookChapterInfo/TlvGuideBookData).
